newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan petrol stations go bust amid price war.
newsitem.headline: More Japan petrol stations go bust amid price war.

text.p: A heated price war amongst Japan's gasoline stations forced 26 stands out of business in 1996, up from nine failures in the previous year, a private credit research company said on Thursday.
Liabilities of the 26 stations reached a combined 4.7 billion yen, a survey by Teikoku Databank Ltd showed.

"Gasoline stations are facing a fierce price war, with newcomers entering the gasoline retail market following the deregulation of oil product imports in April 1996," Teikoku said in a report. "Competition to cut prices is expected to heat up further in 1997," it said.
Gasoline retail prices have plunged in the past two years, squeezing profit margins, as deregulation spurred refiners to cut prices in order to fend off cheap imports.
Competition was also heightened last year as supermarkets entered the retail market.
Japan has about 59,990 gasoline stations nationwide selling a combined 50 million kilolitres of gasoline a year.
Industry analysts expect the number of gasoline stations to fall drastically in coming years.
